en.title: St. Moritz snow forecast next week (23–29 November 2026): 19 cm at the top
en.description: St. Moritz snow forecast for 23–29 November 2026: 19 cm at the top (5–33 cm), 16 cm at the base, snowiest day Wednesday 25 November, with neighbours compared.
en.lede: Next week's snow numbers for St. Moritz: 19 cm at the top, 17 cm at mid-mountain, 16 cm at the base, all as the middle of a range for 23–29 November. The top's range runs from 5 to 33 cm, which says as much as the middle value does.

sections.h: When and where to ski St. Moritz
p: If you can pick one day, take the one that follows Wednesday 25 November, when 8 cm (up to 12 cm) has landed on the upper mountain.

Where to look in St. Moritz: Corviglia's broad slopes, with Corvatsch across the valley for colder north-facing snow. The snow-sure top is Corviglia and Piz Nair above town; the part to treat with caution is the Engadin valley floor, which is already high and dry.
At the top (around 2900 m) the week totals 19 cm, 5–33 cm across our range. Mid-mountain around 2400 m gets 17 cm (5–30 cm), and the base around 1800 m 16 cm (4–28 cm).
The snow is not spread evenly. The days that matter at the top are Wednesday 25 (8 cm, up to 12), Thursday 26 (7 cm, up to 13) and Friday 27 (3 cm, up to 6); the rest of the week is close to dry.
This week gives little here: 9 cm at the top from 17 to 20 November and 4 cm at the base. Next week is the bigger of the two for St. Moritz, which is the reverse of the western Alps.
The base gets nearly as much as the top (16 against 19 cm), which means the snow line stays below the lowest lifts for most of the week. Snow down to the village is the likely picture.
The Engadin is drier than the northern Alps: a modest snowfall here goes a long way in the cold, sunny air.
At the top, next week, our forecast gives Livigno (24 km away) 19 cm, Davos (38 km away) 16 cm and Laax (59 km away) 21 cm, against 19 cm here.
The differences are small: the storm covers this whole corner of the Alps evenly, so pick on terrain and lifts, not on the snow total.

sections.h: The range, not just the number
p: Not very. The high case gives 33 cm up top, the low case just 5 cm, so whether St. Moritz gets a real fall depends on a storm track that is still undecided.
Storm timing tends to firm up first; totals keep moving until a day or two before.

advice: Off the groomed runs, new snow means new avalanche risk: the Swiss avalanche bulletin is the reference.
Check the resort's own opening date and lift status: snow on the mountain does not mean lifts are running.
Plan around the top's 19 cm, and keep the high case of 33 cm as a bonus.
